selection_criteria.question: Does the representation make the high-fragility state change or relation perceptually explicit before algebra?
Can the representation support a controlled picture-to-word-to-symbol-to-equation translation?
Does the representation visibly contradict the dominant SBA04 misconceptions rather than merely annotate them?
Can the representation family preserve one coherent mental model across velocity evolution, direction, speed, symmetry, perpendicularity and height-based speed?

strengths: Makes rising-apex-falling state change and signed vertical velocity visible before equations.
Supports equal-height and height-origin comparisons in the same trajectory geometry.
Provides a stable picture layer from which component symbols and equations can be introduced.
limitations: Direction, magnitude and perpendicular constraints still require local component constructions.

strengths: Strong local bridge from vector geometry to signed components and equations.
Directly supports direction, speed magnitude and dot-product constraints.
limitations: A local triangle-first sequence can hide the temporal rising-apex-falling state model if used as the global primary representation.

strengths: Compactly compares v_x, v_y, speed and direction across named states.
limitations: Compresses trajectory geometry, tangent direction, right-angle relations and height origin into labels rather than perceptual structure.
Encourages lookup before reconstruction for the 20-percent foundation pathway.

decision.rationale: Use the staged trajectory timeline as the global novice-facing spine because it exposes the state evolution and apex distinction before algebra; attach component constructions locally where direction, magnitude, perpendicularity, symmetry and height constraints require stronger mathematical geometry. The state table may be used only as a later consolidation view, not as the primary teaching representation.
